title: Register a name once, on a set that is already synchronized

blocks.text: The page asks: *can you have a race condition without a data race?* Yes. On a `Collections.synchronizedSet`, `contains` and `add` are each synchronized, so there is no data race, but `if (!set.contains(x)) set.add(x)` is still a check-then-act: between the check and the add, another thread may add `x`.

Write `NameRegistry`. Its constructor takes the set to keep names in; the set is thread-safe call by call (like `Collections.synchronizedSet`). `register(name)` returns `true` only for the call that registered the name first, and `false` for every later one. `isRegistered(name)` says whether it is in. Two names are the same name when their text is equal (`equals`), whichever `String` objects carry them.

rows: two threads call `register("eve")` at the same moment

blocks.text: The tests hand you a set whose `add` can be held open, to make two registrations meet in the middle.

cases.says: The first registration of a name succeeds, a repeat is refused, and the name then reads as registered.
When two threads register the same name at once, exactly one of them is told it won.
A name built at run time with the same text as a registered one is the same name: registering it again is refused.

concepts: Individually synchronized calls can still form a race condition when a check and an act are separate calls.
